healthcareSystem: Public healthcare is free for citizens and subsidized for visitors. Seychelles Victoria Hospital is the main facility. Private options are limited on a small island nation. Good basic care for the region. Trilingual (English, French, Seychellois Creole).
qualityNotes: Healthcare is reasonably good for a small island nation. Victoria Hospital on Mahé is well-equipped for basic and moderate conditions. English-speaking doctors and nurses. For complex surgeries or specialized care, patients travel to South Africa, India, or Mauritius. Outer islands (Praslin, La Digue) have clinics but limited capacity.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Victoria open 8:30am-5pm weekdays, 8:30am-12pm Saturdays. Hospital pharmacy open extended hours. Very limited pharmacy access on Praslin and La Digue.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are reasonably stocked with European and Indian medications. Pharmacists speak English, French, and Creole. Bring specialized medications from home as selection is limited on a small island. Behram's Pharmacy in Victoria is the most established.
prescriptionRules: Prescription system exists and is generally enforced. Pharmacists can assist with minor ailments and recommend OTC treatments. Antibiotics require a prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal. Seychelles has strict drug laws with severe penalties.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Strict drug enforcement.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. English documentation is accepted (English is an official language). Keep medications in original packaging. Seychelles has strict drug laws — proper documentation is important.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is important. While basic care is good, complex conditions require evacuation to South Africa or India. Ensure coverage for water sports and diving activities. DAN insurance recommended for divers.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from an endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Seychelles is malaria-free. No special tropical disease risks. Standard travel vaccines recommended.

waterNotes: Tap water on Mahé is treated and generally considered safe, but bottled water is recommended for visitors. Water on Praslin and La Digue may be less reliably treated. Bottled water is widely available at hotels and shops.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are generally good, especially at hotels and restaurants. Fresh seafood is a highlight — eat at reputable restaurants. Creole cuisine is freshly prepared. Exercise normal caution with street food and raw shellfish.
medicalTourismNote: Seychelles is not a medical tourism destination. It is a luxury beach tourism destination with adequate healthcare for visitors.
metaDescription: Health guide for Seychelles: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Seychelles Hospital (Victoria Hospital)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital. Well-equipped for a small island nation. 24/7 emergency department. English, French, and Creole-speaking staff.

hospitals.name: Anse Royale Hospital
hospitals.notes: District hospital on the south side of Mahé. Closer to many beach resorts. Basic emergency care.

hospitals.name: Baie Ste Anne Clinic
hospitals.notes: Health clinic on Praslin. Handles basic medical needs. Serious cases transferred to Mahé by boat or helicopter.

hospitals.name: Logan Hospital (La Digue)
hospitals.notes: Small hospital on La Digue. Basic care only. Serious emergencies require transfer to Mahé.

pharmacyPhrases.local: Mon bezwen medikaman pour douler latet
pharmacyPhrases.transliteration: Mon bez-wen meh-dee-kah-mahn poor doo-lair lah-tet (Seychellois Creole)

dentalCare.availability: Limited but available on Mahé. Victoria Hospital has a dental department. A few private dentists.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is available for basic procedures on Mahé. Limited options on Praslin and La Digue. Quality is reasonable.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, Victoria Hospital has a dental department. Hotels can recommend private dentists on Mahé.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. Some counselors available through the hospital.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited on a small island nation. English-speaking counselors available but scarce. Hotels may be able to assist with referrals. Telehealth from your home country is the best option.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is limited. Many paths and beaches are not wheelchair-accessible. Newer luxury resorts tend to have better accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Victoria Hospital has basic wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses are not wheelchair-accessible. Taxis and hotel transfers are the best option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact resorts in advance about accessibility needs. Some luxury resorts offer accessible rooms and facilities. Beach access is generally challenging. La Digue (mostly bicycles and ox-carts) is particularly difficult for mobility-impaired travelers.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at Victoria Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Seychelles was one of the first countries to achieve high vaccination rates. All restrictions lifted. Tourism is fully operational.

insuranceClaimProcess: Victoria Hospital and private clinics provide English-language receipts. Pay at point of service and claim reimbursement. Some hotels can assist with insurance coordination. Keep all receipts and medical documentation.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Payment in Seychellois rupee. Public hospital charges reduced fees. Seychelles is an expensive destination overall.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Nairobi, Kenya or Johannesburg, South Africa
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation needed for complex surgeries, major trauma, or specialized care. AMREF Flying Doctors operates in the Indian Ocean region. Evacuation from outer islands to Mahé first, then international.

drugNameMap.note: Widely available. Both English and French brand names used.
Available at pharmacies. Useful to carry when island-hopping.
